newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares likely to move sideways to firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares likely to move sideways to firm.

text.p: Singapore shares are likely to move sideways to firmer in quiet trade on Thursday.
"The market is likely to stay neutral awaiting release of key U.S. economic indicators later in the day," one broker said. Blue chips are likely to recover some losses.
"If anything, we expect a rebound in the prices of blue chips because they have already hit the bottom," another broker said.
Malaysian shares traded on Over-the-Counter (OTC) market here are likely to be strong on healthy fundamenals for the Malaysian economy, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the key Straits Times Industrials Index ended down 10.78 points at 2,094.48.
The index fell despite rises in indices tracking blue chips, second line stocks and the Malaysian OTC stocks.

The UOB Blue Chip index was up 0.68 points at 914.52 and the UOB OTC index, tracking mainly Malaysian stocks, was 8.08 points higher at 1,164.76. The UOB SESDAQ index tracking second liners posted the biggest gain, up 1.09 percent, or 0.86 points, at 79.43.
